functions.text: Received word, right-justified (RO1 = LSB); unused high bits low. Float while ROD is high. Not affected by MR.
functions.source: from the TMS 6011 sheet (TI 1975 Semiconductor Memory Data Book, printed pages 152-157, PDF 153-158); the ND manual calls the 6010 equivalent (ND-13.003.01, printed page 59, PDF page 65: 'TMS6010 Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (TMS 6011, AY-5-1012, AY-5-1013)')

functions.text: PE high = parity error; forced low when PI is high. Floats while SFD is high.
functions.source: from the TMS 6011 sheet (TI 1975 Semiconductor Memory Data Book, printed pages 152-157, PDF 153-158); the ND manual calls the 6010 equivalent (ND-13.003.01, printed page 59, PDF page 65: 'TMS6010 Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (TMS 6011, AY-5-1012, AY-5-1013)')

functions.text: FE high = framing error (missing or bad stop bit). Floats while SFD is high.
functions.source: from the TMS 6011 sheet (TI 1975 Semiconductor Memory Data Book, printed pages 152-157, PDF 153-158); the ND manual calls the 6010 equivalent (ND-13.003.01, printed page 59, PDF page 65: 'TMS6010 Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (TMS 6011, AY-5-1012, AY-5-1013)')

functions.text: OE high = overrun (DR not reset before the next word arrived). Floats while SFD is high.
functions.source: from the TMS 6011 sheet (TI 1975 Semiconductor Memory Data Book, printed pages 152-157, PDF 153-158); the ND manual calls the 6010 equivalent (ND-13.003.01, printed page 59, PDF page 65: 'TMS6010 Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (TMS 6011, AY-5-1012, AY-5-1013)')

functions.text: DR high = a word is in the receiver buffer register. DRR low resets it. Floats while SFD is high.
functions.source: from the TMS 6011 sheet (TI 1975 Semiconductor Memory Data Book, printed pages 152-157, PDF 153-158); the ND manual calls the 6010 equivalent (ND-13.003.01, printed page 59, PDF page 65: 'TMS6010 Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (TMS 6011, AY-5-1012, AY-5-1013)')

functions.text: TBRE high = transmitter buffer register empty, ready for a new word. Floats while SFD is high.
functions.source: from the TMS 6011 sheet (TI 1975 Semiconductor Memory Data Book, printed pages 152-157, PDF 153-158); the ND manual calls the 6010 equivalent (ND-13.003.01, printed page 59, PDF page 65: 'TMS6010 Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (TMS 6011, AY-5-1012, AY-5-1013)')

functions.text: TRE high = transmitter has sent a whole word including stop bits; stays high until the next word starts.
functions.source: from the TMS 6011 sheet (TI 1975 Semiconductor Memory Data Book, printed pages 152-157, PDF 153-158); the ND manual calls the 6010 equivalent (ND-13.003.01, printed page 59, PDF page 65: 'TMS6010 Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (TMS 6011, AY-5-1012, AY-5-1013)')

functions.text: Serial out: start bit, 5-8 data bits, optional parity, 1 or 2 stop bits. High when idle; MR sets it high.
functions.source: from the TMS 6011 sheet (TI 1975 Semiconductor Memory Data Book, printed pages 152-157, PDF 153-158); the ND manual calls the 6010 equivalent (ND-13.003.01, printed page 59, PDF page 65: 'TMS6010 Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (TMS 6011, AY-5-1012, AY-5-1013)')

rules: MR high (after power-on): resets status and transmitter registers, TO high; RO not affected.
CRL high loads WLS1, WLS2, PS, PI, SBS into the control register.
Word length WLS1/WLS2: L/L 5, H/L 6, L/H 7, H/H 8 bits.
PS high = even parity, low = odd. PI high = no parity bit (PE forced low). SBS high = 2 stop bits, low = 1.
TBRL low loads TI1..TI8 into the transmitter buffer; TBRL low-to-high moves it into the transmitter register (delayed until the current word is sent).

electrical.notes: P-channel MOS. VSS +5 V +-0.25, VGG -12 V +-0.5, VDD 0 V. VIH VSS-1.5 V min, VIL 0.8 V max. VOL 0.6 V at 1.6 mA, VOH 2.4 V at -200 uA. Inputs have internal pull-ups. Clock 0..200 kHz. TA -25..85 C.

unknown: No TMS6010 datasheet was found. By the owner's ruling (2026-11-23) the file uses the TMS 6011 sheet, which the ND manual names as equivalent. Differences between 6010 and 6011, if any, are unknown.

Reference edges of TI setup/hold (arrows) were lost in the text layer.
notes: ND title also names AY-5-1012 and AY-5-1013 as equivalents.

behaviour.reason: Described from the TMS 6011 sheet (owner's ruling; the ND manual calls the 6010 equivalent). The sheet describes the UART in words (pin functions, control register, word format), which are in pins[].text, functions and state. Two things stop a runnable model in this format: (1) the format has no serial shift engine (a receiver that samples RI at 16 times the bit rate, a transmitter that shifts out start, data, parity and stop bits) - it would need a format addition; (2) the TMS 6011 sheet does not state which edge of TC and RC shifts the data, so it cannot be written without guessing.
